title.narrative: Unlocking the Groundwater Potential of the Kilimanjaro Water Tower (GEF ID 11547)

description.narrative:
The Kilimanjaro Transboundary Aquifer System (KTAS) is a vital water resource shared between Kenya and Tanzania, supporting 2.05 million people. The region faces challenges including inadequate aquifer understanding and governance issues. Through the collaboration of two UN agencies, FAO and UNESCO, a project has been developed to address these challenges through a comprehensive five-year initiative with GEF funding of $7.78 million and $56.5 million in co-financing. This project will address critical groundwater management challenges and enhance water resource sustainability in the Kilimanjaro Transboundary Aquifer System (KTAS).
This regional initiative aims to enhance water security and climate resilience in the Mt. Kilimanjaro region by improving the understanding, governance, and management of the Kilimanjaro Transboundary Aquifer System (KTAS). Key activities include:
- Strengthening transboundary aquifer governance and cooperation; - Conducting comprehensive groundwater resource assessments; - Expanding access to sustainable groundwater resources and protecting recharge areas; - Establishing groundwater management tools and frameworks; and - Engaging stakeholders and promoting knowledge sharing across sectors and scales.
Within the framework of the FAO Global Environmental Facility (GEF) Project Preparation Grant (PPG) for the project “Implementation of the SAP of the Kilimanjaro Transboundary Aquifer: Unlocking the groundwater potential of the Kilimanjaro Water Towers”.
Main Activities:
- Conduct detailed hydrogeological surveys and develop the KTAS conceptual model - Drill exploratory wells and implement managed aquifer recharge plans - Establish groundwater monitoring networks and information management system - Develop a transboundary cooperation framework and Strategic Action Program - Engage stakeholders and implement gender-sensitive M&E system
Expected Outcomes: Improved understanding of KTAS characteristics, enhanced groundwater management capacity, strengthened transboundary cooperation, and increased water security for local communities while protecting ecosystem services.
